key_insight: Early-time mixing in random packed beds is dominated by shear-driven deformation and random overlap of diffusing solute elements, yielding slow concentration-variance decay proportional to t^(-1/2).
engineering_relevance: Shear-induced mixing governs early-stage homogenization of fluid–solid interface reactions in finite packed beds operating at moderate Peclet numbers, Pe = O(10^2).
method: Pore-scale lattice-Boltzmann simulations with Lagrangian particle tracking.
Moving Protean frame analysis to quantify fluid deformation.
Lamellar aggregation model built from Lagrangian kinematics.
evidence_signal: The lamellar aggregation model predicts simulated Eulerian scalar fields well, with early-time variance scaling as σ_c² ∼ Pe^[-α/(2α+1)] t^(-1/2), where α characterizes shear deformation.
watch_item: The shear-dominated scaling applies to an early-time regime under a Peclet-number condition tied to competing deformation timescales; it should not be assumed valid at all times or flow conditions.
paper_title: Finite-time mixing and reaction in packed bed reactors
